about: The edition each ISO/IEC 1989 intrinsic function was INTRODUCED in, derived from the standards themselves and committed because the 2002 and 2009 drafts are not tracked in git (kb/Work PB4296). specs/ISO_COBOL.md is the 2023 text, whose section 8.11 lists names with no edition data and whose Annex E covers only 2014 to 2023, so an introduction year below 2023 can be read only from the older standards' own new-function lists. IntrinsicIntroductionDriftTests holds IntrinsicCatalog's IntroducedIn equal to this file for every clause-15 function, in BOTH directions (a catalog row with no list, a listed name with no catalog row, a name in two lists), and holds the 2023 list equal to Annex E.2 item 13 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md re-read on every run.

editions.source: ISO/IEC 1989:2002 section 8.11 'Intrinsic function names' (76 names) LESS Annex F.2 item 78 (34 names): the 42 functions the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment to ISO 1989:1985 had already defined, i.e. the NIST CCVS85 IF101A-IF142A surface. Derived by set difference from the two lists, and equal to the 42 catalog rows the compiler has always windowed at 85.

ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex F.2 item 78: "Intrinsic functions. New intrinsic functions are:" followed by the 34 names below, ABS first. Corroborated by the same edition's section 8.11 (every one is on its list) and section 15.6 'ABS function'.

ISO/IEC CD 1989 (WG4 committee draft 1.2, 2009) Annex D.2 item 4 'New intrinsic functions': "The intrinsic functions listed below have been introduced in this committee draft International Standard." followed by the 11 names below (kb/Work R28). ABS is not among them.

ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex E.2 item 13 'FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC and new intrinsic functions' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md): the 7 new intrinsic function names. Re-read from the specification on every run by IntrinsicIntroductionDriftTests.
